rationale: Wave 1 of cluster E established six things. (1) Every FL-owned Asia ex-Japan market is gone; Korea is in liquidation. (2) APAC owned stores now means ANZ only: 92 stores, against 103 locator pages and about 88 doors with Christmas seasonal ads; five landlord-confirmed hidden closures. (3) The ANZ legal entities were migrated to new US LLCs, and the legacy NZ and AU entities were struck off after the deal. (4) atmos Japan is flat-to-investing, but its leadership is interim. (5) The Fourlis and Metro Brands licences are growing slowly. (6) About 200 licensed doors are unexplained beyond Alshaya's 40. Wave 2 does not repeat these avenues. It goes after primary documents and modalities wave 1 did not reach: (a) a full ANZ landlord census with quarter dating via Wayback, to test whether APAC closures are running ahead of the 124->122 trend; (b) NZ and AU registry documents (the first FL NZ Holdings LLC accounts, older NZ Inc accounts, ASIC/ABR document lists, NZ PPSR) for post-deal ANZ P&L and any sale preparation; (c) the APAC legal-perimeter wind-down in Singapore, Hong Kong, Korea and Macau through free gazettes and open registries; (d) licensee primary filings for MAP Aktif/MAP Active (the largest unexplained licensed block), Alshaya and the Fourlis Oct-2026 deck, which test the scale and health of the licensing-exit template; (e) atmos ownership and exit-readiness signals from Japanese registers (J-PlatPat assignments, Japan Pension Service insured headcount, founder Hommyo's M&A column and non-compete timing); (f) an ANZ labour and industrial trail (Fair Work Commission, NZ ERA, SDA/First Union), which no cluster has searched. People moves (EMEA GM successor, Robert Fox), Frasers-Accent and European careers and registry work are left to clusters A, B, C, D and F to avoid overlap.

STEPS:
1. Fair Work Commission (https://www.fwc.gov.au).

   - Also search AustLII (https://www.austlii.edu.au) for 'Foot Locker' 2025-2026 across FWC, FCFCOA and state tribunals.
2. New Zealand.
   - Employment Relations Authority determinations (https://determinations.era.govt.nz; search 'Foot Locker'), Employment Court judgments and NZLII for 2024-2026: redundancy, restructure or store-closure references.
   - The Employment NZ collective-agreements data, if searchable.
3. Unions and workers.
   - SDA (sda.org.au, branch sites), RAFFWU (raffwu.org.au) and NZ First Union (firstunion.org.nz): news or member alerts naming Foot Locker in 2025-26 (closure, redundancy, consultation, underpayment, roster cuts).
